ImageDescription.value: Promenade along the Körös, view. In 1890, the Körös-Tisza-Maros Flood Control and Inland Water Regulation Association, based in Szentes, turned to the Ministry of Agriculture due to the gradually rising floods of the Körös, in order to construct the Körös cuttings. At the request of Kunszentmárton, the Körös was left as a living water below the town, and the protective embankment was finally built there. In 1893, the ministry ordered the preparation of a draft for the protective embankment, and in 1895 it was prescribed that the most critical section be reinforced withbrick paving. As a first step, the Gyula-based river engineering office in charge of the works carried out a cutting on the section of the river between Felső-forest and the bridge, and after its construction, began building the protective embankment on October 19, 1897. By mid-February 1898, eight cast iron pipes had been installed to carry away street rainwater, and three concrete pipes to drain the city's inland water. - Based on the contract concluded with Lajos Mátray, master builder and brick manufacturer, on June 16, 1898, the delivery of the ordered bricks (300,000 ordinary semi-acidic, 10,000 wave-breaking, and 10,000 crown bricks) was completed. The masonry work for the pavement construction lasted from August 10 to October 4, 1898. The works were completed on November 24, 1898, by which time the brick pavement stretching from the road bridge to the Gábel pit was also built. On April 21, 2006, the water level peaked at a record level, reaching 1041 cm, making it ultimately necessary to renovate the worn-out protective structures of the 950-meter-long inner-city dike section after the flood receded. The Szeged SZEVIÉP (Szeged Water Construction) company started the work at the beginning of September 2006, during which it reinforced the embankment, replaced the missing brick pavement, raised the crown of the dike, built a reinforced concrete parapet, and established a safer protection system than before. - The current river course of the Hármas-Körös was only reached about 6-7,000 years ago. - From Öcsöd, the Körös occupied the former bed of the Tisza, and the two rivers merged at Csongrád, forming the currently existing Tiszazug. The remnants of the Tisza fundamentally determined the bed of the Hármas-Körös and theriver's water level. This is clearly noticeable around Kunszentmárton and Szelevény, where the Tisza, the Körös, and the Hortobágy separated, and their former riverbeds cut off by river regulation embrace into a huge labyrinth. The Hármas-Körös and its floodplain that run alongside the townare part of the Körös-Maros National Park. The flora and fauna of this warm, dry climate area are very rich, providing an inexhaustible research environment for experts. The units of the National Park are framed by the Körös rivers from the north, the Maros River from the south, and the Tisza River from the east. Today, the Körös rivers' water system represents a secondary landscape. The declaration of the Hármas-Körös as a protected area began at the end of the 1970s and took place in several phases. The Körös floodplain (from the confluence ofthe Kettős-Körös and the Sebes-Körös up to Szelevény) covers 6,579 hectares as a territorial unit of the Körös-Maros National Park. In the times before river regulation, the landscape bordered by the Tisza and its tributaries was made up of an extremely varied mosaic of wet and drier types of habitats (salt meadows, salt oak woods, loess steppes, marshes, swamps, oxbow lakes, wet meadows, hard- and softwood gallery forests and groves). - The floodplain forests have two characteristic types: the more common willow-poplar softwood gallery forest, the shrubby willows, and the now rarer hard-wood gallery forest of oak-ash-elm found on drier high ridges. A distinctive feature of the floodplain forests is the climbing of hops and wild grape on the trees; the floodplain meadows and pastures, scissorgrass meadows, as well as the salt meadows with limestone grass communities are also significant. Larger populations of plants such as fox sedge, bulrush species, water caltrop, and yellow iris still live here. Among its mammals, the otter deserves mention; among its birds, the nesting purple heron and little egret, as well as the yellow-eyed marsh owl. In the floodplain forests, herons, long-eared owls and tawny owls live, while in more open parts, hoopoes and bee-eaters can be found. In the reeds, the reed bunting, the reed, marsh, and reed warblers, as well as the spotted, chattering, and singing reed warblers, are common. - Alsó Köröspart Street (lit. Lower Körös Shore Street), Kunszentmárton, Jász-Nagykun-Szolnok County, Hungary.

ImageDescription.value: 'Körösvölgyi Állatpark' lit.: Körös Valley Animal Park (Est 2014). In fact it is the park of the Csáky Mansion, a showcase located in Anna Grove, filled with century-old trees. The main building houses a total of 7,000-liter aquarium with the fish of our domestic waters. In the park of Anna Park, along a 2,100-meter-long promenade, aviaries, predator houses, a fenced wetland habitat, a squirrel house, and large enclosures provide homes for more than 50 species of animals, numbering several hundred individuals. There is a petting zoo, and the Kid's Corner playground. The permanent exhibition 'Natural Treasures of Körös-Maros National Park' can be seen on two levels. In the nature protected park are multiple buildings. Now here is the Visitor Centre of the Körös-Maros National Park. The main building of THE mansion now HQ of the Körös-Maros National Park. Built in 1908. Built to Count Albin Csáky. Planned and built by local builder master János Bányász. - The Csáky mansion and its park is local grade listed. - Anna-liget (Anna Grove) Road, Szarvas, Békés County, Hungary.
